checks.finding: Every REQ-001..REQ-006 (including REQ-003's eight lettered sub-checks a-h) states a concrete, measurable shape or behavior (e.g. REQ-001's exact object required-lists and enum values; REQ-002's operator-by-operator fail-closed/exists-exception truth table; REQ-003(a-h)'s eight independently identifiable checks; REQ-004's fragment-selection API and stable-sort rule; REQ-005's header/`--check`/discovery-fallback contract), and each is matched to fixture-driven ACs in acceptance-tests.md (AC-001..AC-033) that name the exact diagnostic string or observable outcome expected. No in-scope requirement is stated only as vague intent.

requirements.md's six Goals bullets (REQ-001..REQ-006) each map to a contiguous AC block in acceptance-tests.md: REQ-001->AC-001..AC-006, REQ-002->AC-007..AC-013, REQ-003(a-h)->AC-014..AC-022 (one AC per lettered sub-check), REQ-004->AC-023/AC-024, REQ-005->AC-025..AC-029, REQ-006->AC-030..AC-033. acceptance-tests.md's own header states this 1:1 renumbering was done specifically to close a prior adversarial-review Blocker finding ('AC-TEST 1:1 is false'), and the Requirement column in the AC-TEST table cross-confirms every mapping.

Acceptance criteria consistently describe concrete fixture inputs and expected diagnostics/outputs rather than intent, e.g. AC-014 ('two gates[] entries sharing one id fails validation with a gate-id-duplicate diagnostic'), AC-024 (reordered/duplicated ID lists must produce an identical digest; an absent ID is a hard failure), AC-026 ('a hand-mutated committed projection causes --check to exit non-zero... no filesystem write occurs'). AC-034/AC-035, which are manual/procedural rather than automated, still name an externally observable check (git status/diff confined to specs/, a grep/cross-reference audit) rather than vague intent.

requirements.md's Non-goals section lists seven explicit exclusions with citations: no Epic A1 deliverables, no Epic A5 Resolver/Facet-Manifest work, no Capability Pack content authoring, no freezing of upgrade_reasons/delivery_strategy.kind vocabulary, no Artifact/Promotion Gate stage implementation, no new plugin introduction, no actual plugin/contract/test file writes in this commit, and no tasks.md/traceability.md authoring or workflow-state-registry.json registration in this commit -- each with a stated rationale (e.g. check-workflow-state.sh:681-682's hard-enforcement). This closes off the areas where the feature could otherwise expand.

Material constraints are stated explicitly: a hard external dependency and its blocked-until-condition (Dependencies section, Epic A1 canonicalizer path/version/I-O contract, REQ-004 'implementation task is blocked'); a security/compatibility boundary (Provider-name contamination check, ADR-0018, REQ-003(g)/AC-020); an approval boundary (Roles and Permissions: Spec-Review-Status/Impl-Review-Status stay Pending for a human, guard-invariants protected-file changes require human cp + MANIFEST.sha256 verification, AC-029); and a migration/registration constraint (workflow-state-registry.json registration deferred to a separate commit, Non-goals).

The highest-risk claims each have a named validation surface: the Epic A1 external-dependency risk has AC-023/TEST-023 explicitly marked 'Planned (blocked on Epic A1's canonicalizer contract...)'; the cross-runtime determinism claim has AC-031/AC-033 golden-fixture and 3-runtime parity locks; the first automated Provider-neutrality enforcement (INV-008, previously only a human review policy) has AC-020's per-category negative fixtures; and the protected-file/guard-invariants registration risk has AC-029's three-part human-copy verification procedure. No high-risk claim in this package is left without a stated acceptance criterion, fixture target, or manual-review record.
